segments.intent: Summarize flipper length and body mass by species and sex
segments.value:
```sql
SELECT
  species,
  sex,
  COUNT(*) AS penguin_count,
  AVG(flipper_length_mm) AS avg_flipper_length_mm,
  MIN(flipper_length_mm) AS min_flipper_length_mm,
  MAX(flipper_length_mm) AS max_flipper_length_mm,
  AVG(body_mass_g) AS avg_body_mass_g,
  MIN(body_mass_g) AS min_body_mass_g,
  MAX(body_mass_g) AS max_body_mass_g
FROM penguins
GROUP BY species, sex
ORDER BY species, sex
```

segments.content:
Here’s a grouped summary by species and sex for **flipper length** and **body mass**. | Species | Sex | Count | Avg flipper length (mm) | Flipper range (mm) | Avg body mass (g) | Body mass range (g) | |---|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---| | Adelie | female | 73 | 187.8 | 172–202 | 3368.8 | 2850–3900 | | Adelie | male | 73 | 192.4 | 178–210 | 4043.5 | 3325–4775 | | Chinstrap | female | 34 | 191.7 | 178–202 | 3527.2 | 2700–4150 | | Chinstrap | male | 34 | 199.9 | 187–212 | 3939.0 | 3250–4800 | | Gentoo | female | 58 | 212.7 | 203–222 | 4679.7 | 3950–5200 | | Gentoo | male | 61 | 221.5 | 208–231 | 5484.8 | 4750–6300 | A few clear patterns: - **Gentoo** penguins are the largest on both measures: longest flippers and highest body mass. - **Adelie** are generally the smallest. - Within each species, **males are heavier and have longer flippers than females** on average. - **Chinstrap** tend to fall between Adelie and Gentoo. There are also a few rows with **missing sex values**, so I excluded those from the table above.
